name: AI News
blurb: Daily AI news from the publishers who broke it, split into headline coverage of the field and vendor announcements from the companies building it. Every story links to the original source, and any claim quoted in our coverage is cross-referenced against the laws, lawsuits, companies, tools, papers, and people already tracked in this atlas.

domains.name: AI Headline News
domains.blurb: The day's most consequential AI stories across law, policy, research, safety, and society, curated from 34 vetted feeds. Each item carries the original publisher link and a note on how it connects to the bills, cases, and frameworks tracked elsewhere on this site.

domains.name: AI Vendor News
domains.blurb: Product launches, model releases, pricing changes, and company announcements from the AI vendors themselves. Each item links to the vendor's original announcement and cross-references the company's profile in our AI Companies directory where one exists.

domains.name: This Week in AI
domains.blurb: A weekly record of what moved in AI policy and litigation, permalinked by ISO week.

domains.name: AI Historical Timeline
domains.blurb: From the 1940s to the present: Turing, the perceptron, expert systems, backpropagation, deep learning, AlexNet, transformers, and what followed.

reading.body:
Daily AI news tracked against legal, policy, and research developments shows which announcements carry real regulatory or capability consequences and which do not.

The news section separates vendor announcements from field coverage, a distinction that matters because they measure different things. Vendor news tracks product releases and pricing as they happen. Headline news connects the day's stories to bills, lawsuits, and frameworks already in motion elsewhere on this site. This separation lets readers see when a company announcement triggers regulatory response, when research papers shift policy thinking, or when legal action follows a capability claim.

The cross-referencing against tracked laws, cases, and people means claims get checked against their actual source. A vendor's statement about a model's performance can be measured against the research that supports it. A policy announcement can be traced to the bill or regulation behind it. This matters for compute and infrastructure because many AI announcements concern resource allocation, data center permits, or power contracts, and the legal and policy context determines whether those projects proceed.

The coverage spans 34 vetted feeds for headline news but only one page of vendor announcements so far. This reflects the current state of the field: most consequential AI developments appear in research, policy, and litigation first, with vendor news following or responding. The historical timeline going back to the 1940s exists but contains no pages yet, so readers cannot yet see how today's news fits into longer patterns of AI capability and constraint.
